newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to sell 40 pct of Tyumen Oil Company.
newsitem.headline: Russia to sell 40 pct of Tyumen Oil Company.

text.p: Russia is holding an investment tender for 40 percent of Tyumenskaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (TNK) (Tyumen Oil), the Federal Property Fund said on Tuesday.

The minimum investment is $160 million over two years, fund spokesman Vladimir Yefimchik told Reuters. Bids must be received by July 16 and the results will be decided on July 18. Banks and foreign investors are not eligible to bid.
The fixed price for the 40 percent stake, which comprises 632.66 million shares, each with a face value of five roubles, is 145 billion roubles ($25 million).

TNK's pre-tax profit fell to 200.6 billion roubles on a Russian accounts accruals basis in 1996 from 486.6 billion in 1995. Sales rose to 14.27 trillion roubles from 11.99 trillion. Production fell to 21.30 million tonnes from 22.57 million.
TNK is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating unit is Nizhnevartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS.
The Russian government holds 99.98 percent of TNK.
Former Fuel and Energy Minister Yuri Shafranik is board chairman both of TNK and of the Central Fuel Company, which is based in Moscow.
